text:
GENERATE BURST CS-vfx-zeus-sheets — greyscale PAINTED-PIXEL effect sheets for ZEUS CHAIN LIGHTNING (breadth test kit 5: hades1-zeus-chain; style card v0.2). task_id "CS-vfx-zeus-sheets".

Paint ONE 1536×1024 image on flat PURE BLACK #000000 — the background is a BLACK VOID: NO grey fog, NO gradient, NO vignette, NO atmosphere, NO lighting on the background; every background pixel is exactly #000000 (this is the one hard rule; a grey or hazy background is a failed image). The flask glass is drawn MID GREY so it stays visible against black. a 6-column × 4-row grid of 256×256 cells (each effect drawing centred in its cell, never touching the cell edge), GREYSCALE ONLY (light grey → mid grey → dark grey → darker grey (use pure WHITE only for the tiniest fuse spark and the very centre of the flame cores, never for whole shapes), no colour), in a PAINTED-PIXEL register: each drawing looks like a hand-painted sprite at a small native size — hard-edged shapes, 3–4 flat value steps, a near-white core, dark grey rim/interior holes, ABSOLUTELY NO soft gradients, NO glow, NO haze, NO bloom, NO radial light falloff around any shape, NO blur, NO anti-aliasing, NO outline strokes: every pixel is one of exactly FIVE values — pure black background, dark grey #404040, mid grey #808080, light grey #C0C0C0, pure white #FFFFFF — with hard, stair-stepped edges as if drawn with a 1-px pencil at 64 px and scaled up 4x with nearest-neighbour. Think 1990s 16-bit sprite effects (Diablo I / Secret of Mana spell sprites) drawn in greyscale, NOT a modern glowing render. If you are tempted to make anything glow, draw a ring of light-grey pixels instead. Design it as a divine chain-lightning effect (a thunderhead charge, a thick forked bolt that JUMPS between points, a bright branching strike with a small halo ring, lingering sparks) even though it is greyscale; bolts thicker and more ornamental than plain lightning, with hard pixel steps.
ROW 1 — CAST (6 frames): a small storm-cloud curl forming above a point with arcs crackling downward, growing to a bright charged knot; frame 6 the knot flares with 3 short forks.
ROW 2 — TRAVEL (6 frames): a thick forked chain-bolt segment drawn facing RIGHT with one clear JUMP kink in the middle and short branches, sparks trailing LEFT; each frame a different path so they loop.
ROW 3 — IMPACT (6 frames): the chain strikes: frame 1 a small bright branching star (no white disc); then a ring of 6–8 thick forks bursting outward with a thin halo ring; then the forks thin and the ring breaks into sparks; the last frame is drifting sparks.
ROW 4 — RESIDUAL + SPARK (6 frames): frames 1–4: a flat scorched ground ring (an ellipse wider than tall) with small arcs jumping across it, four looping variations of the same size; frames 5–6: one single thick spark fragment facing RIGHT, two variants.
Every drawing must read at 25 % size (64 px cells). Nothing between cells; no labels, grid lines, text or border; background pure black.

One image_gen call. ONE retry only if colour appears, any glow/haze/gradient appears, cells bleed into each other, or a row is missing — name the reason. Copy the output from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/zeus_sheets.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "CS-vfx-zeus-sheets"; images = the file with prompt, references and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.
